The Fligner--Killeen and Levene tests compare residual [variances](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
across the levels of a grouping variable.
The [Breusch--Pagan test](#def-breusch-pagan) instead asks
whether the error variance changes
with the [covariates](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-predictors) themselves,
which can be continuous
[@breusch1979simple].

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-auxiliary-regression}
#### Auxiliary regression

Let $\resid_1, \ldots, \resid_n$ be the [residuals](#def-resid-fitted)
from a fitted [linear regression model](#def-lm-general-form),
and let $z_i$ be a vector of $q$ covariates for observation $i$
(by default, the model's own predictors, without the intercept).

The **auxiliary regression** is the ordinary least-squares regression
of the squared residuals $\resid_i^2$ on $z_i$, with an intercept;
let $R^2_{\text{aux}}$ be its [coefficient of determination](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/correlation-regression.html#def-r-squared).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-breusch-pagan}
#### Studentized Breusch--Pagan statistic

With $R^2_{\text{aux}}$ the coefficient of determination of the auxiliary regression (@def-auxiliary-regression),
the **studentized Breusch--Pagan statistic**
[@koenker1981note] is:

$$
\text{BP} \eqdef n R^2_{\text{aux}}
$$ {#eq-breusch-pagan-stat}
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-breusch-pagan-original}
#### Original Breusch--Pagan statistic

In contrast to @eq-breusch-pagan-stat, the **original Breusch--Pagan statistic**
[@breusch1979simple]
uses $\esig^2 \eqdef \frac{1}{n}\sumin \resid_i^2$
and regresses $g_i \eqdef \resid_i^2 / \esig^2$ on $z_i$;
the statistic is half of that regression's explained sum of squares.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-breusch-pagan-null}
#### Null distribution of the Breusch--Pagan statistic

Under the [null hypothesis](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-null-hypothesis) that the error variance is constant,
$\Var{Y_i \mid z_i} = \sigma^2$ for every $i$,
both versions of the Breusch--Pagan statistic
are approximately $\chi^2_q$ in large samples.
The original version also assumes Gaussian errors
[@breusch1979simple];
the studentized version does not
[@koenker1981note].
:::

::: notes
The proof uses large-sample score-test theory,
which is beyond the scope of these notes;
see @breusch1979simple and @koenker1981note.

The null hypothesis concerns the errors, not the residuals:
even when the error variance is constant,
the residual variances differ with [leverage](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-leverage)
(@eq-var-resid-leverage).
:::

Large values of the statistic,
and small [p-values](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-p-value),
suggest that the error variance changes with $z_i$.
